## Abstract
This report describes ENA study PRJEB1234, retrieved through the BRC Analytics ENA proxy. The study, titled "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome" (secondary accession ERP002070), was first made public on 2013-06-06. The study contains 916 sequencing runs derived from two grass species: *Setaria italica* (foxtail millet, NCBI taxid 4555) and *Setaria viridis* (green foxtail). A sampled inspection of 28 runs shows uniform library characteristics: paired-end whole-genome shotgun (WGS) sequencing from genomic DNA, prepared with random selection and sequenced on the Illumina Genome Analyzer platform. Sample titles follow a consistent "Worldwide foxtail millet accession CiNNN" naming scheme, consistent with a diversity-panel resequencing project supporting a haplotype map. Per-run read counts across the sampled runs range from roughly 3.4×10⁵ to 3.1×10⁶ paired reads (≈6.5×10⁷ to ≈6.0×10⁸ bases). Files are available as gzipped FASTQ through the ENA FTP/HTTPS mirrors. Because the total number of runs (916) exceeds the response size limit, only 28 of the 916 records were returned in this query; the summary of run-level attributes is therefore based on that sample, while the study-level counts (916 runs, two organisms, 2013-06-06 release date) are reported directly by the ENA endpoint and cover the full study.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** ENA study PRJEB1234 (secondary accession ERP002070) is a plant population-genomics dataset focused on foxtail millet (*Setaria italica*) and its wild relative *Setaria viridis*. Foxtail millet is a diploid C4 cereal used as a model for grass genomics and as a food/feed crop. A "haplotype map" implies resequencing of many accessions to catalog segregating variation.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** The user asked what the study contains; the composition, size, sequencing design, and organisms of PRJEB1234 were unknown at the outset of the query.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: describe the contents of ENA study PRJEB1234 — title, release date, organisms, number of runs, and the sequencing design used. No statistical hypothesis applies.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** A single-study lookup in ENA. The BRC Analytics ENA proxy was chosen because it accepts ENA/SRA study accessions directly and returns study metadata together with per-run records and download links.

**Materials.** European Nucleotide Archive (ENA), queried through the `brc_ena_study` tool.

**Procedures.**
1. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJEB1234")` — one call, returning the study record and per-run metadata.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistical modeling was performed. The run total (916) and the organism list are reported by the ENA `filereport` endpoint at the study level. Library-design attributes were tabulated from the 28 run records returned; the tool explicitly flagged that the response was size-capped at 28 of 916 runs, so run-level attributes are a sample, not a census.

## III. Results

**Table 1. Study-level metadata for PRJEB1234.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Study accession | PRJEB1234 |
| Secondary study accession | ERP002070 |
| Study title | A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome |
| First public | 2013-06-06 |
| Organisms in runs | *Setaria italica*, *Setaria viridis* |
| Total runs | 916 |
| Runs returned in this response | 28 (size-capped) |

**Table 2. Library and platform attributes across the 28 returned runs.**

| Attribute | Value observed (28/28 runs) |
|---|---|
| Library strategy | WGS |
| Library source | GENOMIC |
| Library selection | RANDOM |
| Library layout | PAIRED |
| Instrument platform | ILLUMINA |
| Instrument model | Illumina Genome Analyzer |
| Scientific name (in sampled runs) | *Setaria italica* (tax_id 4555) |
| Sample title pattern | "Worldwide foxtail millet accession Ci###" |

**Table 3. Read-count range across the 28 returned runs.**

| Metric | Minimum | Maximum |
|---|---|---|
| read_count (paired reads) | 342,997 (ERR214785) | 3,138,052 (ERR214778) |
| base_count | 65,169,430 | 596,229,880 |

**Findings.** PRJEB1234 is a foxtail-millet resequencing study released on 2013-06-06, comprising 916 sequencing runs spanning two organisms (*S. italica* and *S. viridis*). All 28 runs inspected are paired-end Illumina Genome Analyzer WGS libraries prepared with random genomic selection, and all 28 are labeled *S. italica* accessions of the "Ci###" series. Per-run yields in the sampled subset span roughly an order of magnitude (≈0.34–3.14 million paired reads; ≈65–596 Mb). FASTQ files are available via ENA FTP/HTTPS (e.g., `https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR214/ERR214766/…`).

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The metadata are consistent with a diversity-panel resequencing project that assembles a haplotype map from many *S. italica* accessions, with *S. viridis* runs likely serving as a wild-relative outgroup or comparator. Uniform WGS/PAIRED/Illumina design across all sampled runs supports downstream variant calling and haplotype construction.

**Context.** No linked publications were retrieved in this query, so authorship and study rationale are not attributed here.

**Limitations.** The ENA endpoint returned 28 of 916 runs before the response was trimmed. Attributes such as "all runs are paired-end WGS on Illumina Genome Analyzer" are therefore descriptive of the sample of 28 and not verified across the full 916. The tool also warned that a project-level organism label is not the organism of every run; the presence of *S. viridis* in `organisms_in_runs` confirms this, and none of the 28 returned runs were *S. viridis*, so the split between the two organisms cannot be quantified from this response. Collection dates were empty in every returned run. No sample-attribute metadata (geography, phenotype) were fetched.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** PRJEB1234 is a 916-run *Setaria* WGS resequencing study underpinning a foxtail-millet haplotype map. To complete the picture, next queries worth running: (i) `brc_ena_runs(taxonomy_id="4555", …)` and equivalent for *S. viridis* (taxid 4556) to page through all 916 runs and tally the two organisms; (ii) `ncbi_find_uids(db="bioproject", accessions="PRJEB1234")` followed by `ncbi_linked_records(from_db="bioproject", to_dbs="pubmed", …)` to retrieve any associated publication; (iii) `ncbi_biosample_metadata` on a subset of SAMEA accessions to recover geographic origin and phenotype for the "Ci###" accessions.

## References
[1] European Nucleotide Archive, study report endpoint. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=PRJEB1234

## Acknowledgments
Data provided by the European Nucleotide Archive (EMBL-EBI). Retrieval mediated by the BRC Analytics ENA proxy.
